objects.description: Incomplete forward usage of struct mallinfo as returned by h_mallinfo and used in several Android-specific functions. The full layout is not defined in this header; it relies on the libc-provided definition from malloc.h/glibc or bionic. Treat as an opaque C struct here since only the type name appears; details are unknown in this header.

functions.name: h_malloc
functions.description: Allocate a new heap block of at least size bytes. Returns a pointer to the allocated memory or NULL on failure. Usage mirrors standard malloc.
requirements: size may be 0; behavior follows allocator semantics (may return NULL or a unique pointer)
Returned pointer must be freed with h_free or h_free_sized
Do not pass the returned pointer (or any interior pointer) to non-matching deallocation functions

functions.name: h_calloc
functions.description: Allocate zero-initialized storage for an array of nmemb elements of size bytes each. Returns a pointer or NULL on failure. Usage mirrors standard calloc.
requirements: If nmemb*size overflows size_t, allocation fails (implementation-defined)
Returned pointer must be freed with h_free or h_free_sized
Zero-initialization applies to the full requested size

functions.name: h_realloc
functions.description: Resize the allocation pointed to by ptr to size bytes, preserving existing data up to the lesser of old and new sizes. Behaves like standard realloc.
requirements: If ptr is NULL, behaves like h_malloc(size)
If size is 0 and ptr is not NULL, it may free ptr and return NULL or a unique pointer (implementation-defined)
ptr must be a pointer returned by this allocator (or NULL) and not previously freed
Returned pointer (when non-NULL) must be freed with h_free or h_free_sized

functions.name: h_aligned_alloc
functions.description: Allocate size bytes with a specified alignment. Mirrors C11 aligned_alloc: alignment must be a valid power-of-two and size must be a multiple of alignment.
requirements: alignment must be a power of two
size must be a multiple of alignment
On failure returns NULL
Returned pointer must be freed with h_free or h_free_sized

functions.name: h_free
functions.description: Deallocate a block previously returned by h_malloc/h_calloc/h_realloc/h_aligned_alloc (or compatible allocation functions). Safe to pass NULL.
requirements: ptr must be either NULL or a pointer previously returned by this allocator and not yet freed
Do not double-free or free interior pointers
After return, ptr must not be used

functions.name: h_posix_memalign
functions.signature: int h_posix_memalign(void **memptr, size_t alignment, size_t size);
functions.description: Allocate size bytes aligned to alignment and store the result in *memptr. Returns 0 on success; on failure, returns an error code and leaves *memptr unspecified. Mirrors POSIX posix_memalign.
requirements: memptr must be non-NULL and point to writable storage for a void*
alignment must be a power of two and a multiple of sizeof(void*)
On success, *memptr must be freed with h_free or h_free_sized
On failure, return value is nonzero (e.g., EINVAL for invalid alignment, ENOMEM for allocation failure)

functions.name: h_malloc_usable_size
functions.description: Return the usable size of the allocation pointed to by ptr, which may be equal to or larger than the requested size. Mirrors malloc_usable_size semantics.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer to a currently allocated heap block obtained from this allocator
Passing invalid or non-allocated pointers results in undefined behavior

functions.name: h_mallopt
functions.description: Adjust allocator tunables identified by param to value. Mirrors glibc mallopt; available options are implementation-specific.
requirements: param and value must be valid for this allocator; unsupported values cause failure (return 0)
Call effects and applicability are implementation-defined; callers should handle a 0 return as failure and 1 as success

functions.name: h_malloc_trim
functions.description: Attempt to release free memory back to the system, keeping at least pad bytes of free space in the allocator. Mirrors malloc_trim.
requirements: pad is a non-negative size specifying how much free space to retain
Return value nonzero on success, zero on failure (implementation-defined)

functions.name: h_malloc_stats
functions.description: Print allocator statistics to stderr. Mirrors malloc_stats.
requirements: Produces output to stderr; no return value
May be expensive; intended for diagnostics only

functions.name: h_malloc_info
functions.description: Write allocator state in XML to the given FILE stream. Mirrors glibc malloc_info. Declared only when not building for Android.
requirements: Available only when __ANDROID__ is not defined
fp must be a valid, open FILE* for writing
options usage is implementation-defined (commonly 0)
Returns 0 on success, nonzero on error (implementation-defined)

functions.name: h_memalign
functions.description: Obsolete/legacy function to allocate size bytes with a given alignment. Mirrors glibc memalign; similar to aligned_alloc but with different historical constraints.
requirements: alignment must be a power of two and typically a multiple of sizeof(void*)
On failure returns NULL
Returned pointer must be freed with h_free or h_free_sized
Function is obsolete; prefer h_aligned_alloc or h_posix_memalign

functions.name: h_valloc
functions.description: Obsolete function that allocates size bytes aligned to the system page size. Mirrors glibc valloc.
requirements: Available only when not building for Android
On failure returns NULL
Returned pointer must be freed with h_free or h_free_sized

functions.name: h_pvalloc
functions.description: Obsolete function that allocates at least size bytes, rounding the allocation size up to a multiple of the system page size, and page-aligns the result. Mirrors glibc pvalloc.
requirements: Available only when not building for Android
On failure returns NULL
Returned pointer must be freed with h_free or h_free_sized

functions.name: h_cfree
functions.description: Obsolete synonym for free. Provided on glibc systems. Safe to pass NULL.
requirements: Available only when __GLIBC__ is defined
ptr must be NULL or a pointer previously returned by this allocator and not yet freed

functions.name: h_malloc_get_state
functions.description: Return an opaque representation of the allocator state for later restoration. Mirrors glibc malloc_get_state.
requirements: Available only when __GLIBC__ is defined
The returned buffer must later be passed to h_malloc_set_state; ownership and lifetime are implementation-defined

functions.name: h_malloc_set_state
functions.description: Restore allocator state from a buffer previously returned by h_malloc_get_state. Mirrors glibc malloc_set_state.
requirements: Available only when __GLIBC__ is defined
state must be a buffer previously obtained from h_malloc_get_state without modification
Return value indicates success (non-negative) or failure (implementation-defined)

functions.name: h_mallinfo_narenas
functions.description: Android extension returning the number of arenas used by the allocator.
requirements: Available only when __ANDROID__ is defined

functions.name: h_mallinfo_nbins
functions.description: Android extension returning the number of bins used by the allocator.
requirements: Available only when __ANDROID__ is defined

functions.name: h_malloc_iterate
functions.signature: int h_malloc_iterate(uintptr_t base, size_t size, void (*callback)(uintptr_t ptr, size_t size, void *arg), void *arg);
functions.description: Android extension to iterate over allocations in the specified address range [base, base+size), invoking callback for each object. Returns 0 on success, nonzero on error (implementation-defined).
requirements: Available only when __ANDROID__ is defined
callback must be a valid function pointer; arg is user data passed to callback
base and size define the range to scan; specifics of coverage and concurrency are implementation-defined

functions.name: h_malloc_disable
functions.description: Android extension that disables the allocator (typically to make heap operations fail or pause) for diagnostic purposes.
requirements: Available only when __ANDROID__ is defined
Intended for diagnostic/profiling; exact effects are implementation-defined

functions.name: h_malloc_enable
functions.description: Android extension that re-enables the allocator after h_malloc_disable.
requirements: Available only when __ANDROID__ is defined
Must be called after h_malloc_disable to resume normal operation

functions.name: h_malloc_disable_memory_tagging
functions.description: Android extension to disable memory tagging, if supported by the platform.
requirements: Available only when __ANDROID__ is defined
Has effect only on platforms/runtimes that support memory tagging; otherwise a no-op

functions.name: h_malloc_object_size
functions.description: Return an upper bound on the size of the allocation that contains ptr, based on malloc metadata. Useful for bounds checks and diagnostics.
requirements: ptr must point within or to the start of a currently allocated object managed by this allocator
Passing invalid pointers results in undefined behavior

functions.name: h_malloc_object_size_fast
functions.description: Like h_malloc_object_size but avoids locking, so results are more limited and may be conservative. Intended for fast-path checks.
requirements: ptr must point within or to the start of a currently allocated object managed by this allocator
May return a less precise upper bound than h_malloc_object_size

functions.name: h_free_sized
functions.description: Free with an extra parameter supplying the originally requested allocation size. This allocator uses the size for security checks to verify it matches the allocated size.
requirements: ptr must be NULL or a pointer previously returned by this allocator and not yet freed
expected_size must match the originally requested allocation size for ptr; a mismatch may trigger security checks and failure/abort (implementation-defined)
Do not use after free
